# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

```plantuml
class AutoPruneStrategy {
    addNodeAndUpdateBranch(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>) : void
    addNodeToTree(node : ChainNode, currentBranch : List<TreeNode>, currentNodeRef : node) : void
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode
    isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(queue : Deque) : void
}

    content : String
    levelSeq : List<int>
    levelText : String
    title : String
    concatNode(node : BaseNode) : void
}
class ChainNode {
    patternPriority : int
}

    patterns : List<LevelPattern>
    createChainNode(levelSeq : List<int>, title : String, content : String, levelText : String, patternPriority : int) : ChainNode
    detectLevel(line : String) : ChainNode
    parseToChain(text : String) : List<ChainNode>
}

    description : String
    failOnConvert : boolean
    fixedLevelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>

    minLevel : int
    numberType : NumberType

    separator : String

    getRegex() : Pattern

    separator : String

    validate() : void
}
class StrictStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    createTreeNode(chainnode : ChainNode) : TreeNode

}

    strategy : TreeBuildingStrategy

}
abstract class TreeBuildingStrategy {
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    getLastLevel(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : int
    getPrefix(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : List<EIntegerObject>
    isImmNext(frontSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, backSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
    isRoot(node : BaseNode) : boolean
}
class TreeExporter {
    escapeJson(s : String) : String
    exportChain(chain : List<ChainNode>) : String
    exportToJson(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportToJsonFile(tree : TreeNode, filePath : Path) : void
    exportTree(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportTreeInternal(node : TreeNode, prefix : String, isLast : boolean, isRoot : boolean) : String
    nodeToDict(node : TreeNode) : EMap
    toJson(obj : EJavaObject, indent : int) : String
}
class TreeNode {
    children : List<TreeNode>
    parent : TreeNode
    addChild(child : TreeNode) : void
    getFullContent() : String
    mergeAllChildren() : void
}
enum NumberType {
    ARABIC
    ROMAN
    CHINESE
    LETTER
    CIRCLED
}

TreeNode --> TreeNode : parent  'opposite: children
```

```plantuml
    buildTree(chain : List<ChainNode>) : TreeNode
    getLastLevel(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : int
    getPrefix(levelSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : List<EIntegerObject>
    isImmNext(frontSeq : List<EIntegerObject>, backSeq : List<EIntegerObject>) : boolean
    isRoot(node : BaseNode) : boolean
}
class TreeExporter {
    escapeJson(s : String) : String
    exportChain(chain : List<ChainNode>) : String
    exportToJson(tree : TreeNode) : String
    exportToJsonFile(tree : TreeNode, filePath : Path) : void

    exportTreeInternal(node : TreeNode, prefix : String, isLast : boolean, isRoot : boolean) : String
    nodeToDict(node : TreeNode) : EMap
    toJson(obj : EJavaObject, indent : int) : String
}
class TreeNode {
    children : List<TreeNode>
    parent : TreeNode
    addChild(child : TreeNode) : void
    getFullContent() : String
    mergeAllChildren() : void
}
enum NumberType {
    ARABIC
    ROMAN
    CHINESE
    LETTER
    CIRCLED
}

AutoPruneStrategy --|> TreeBuildingStrategy
ChainNode --|> BaseNode
ChainParser *-- "*" LevelPattern : patterns
LevelPattern --> ParserHelper : helper
StrictStrategy --|> TreeBuildingStrategy
TreeBuilder --> TreeBuildingStrategy : strategy
TreeNode --|> BaseNode
TreeNode *-- "*" TreeNode : children  'opposite: parent
TreeNode --> TreeNode : parent  'opposite: children
@enduml
```

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

```text
When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.
```

# Operation Specifications
AutoPruneStrategy::buildTree
Summary: Constructs the full document outline tree from a chain of heading nodes using the auto-prune
         tolerant strategy that recovers from irregular level jumps and handles a bounded pending queue.
Algorithm:
  1. If chain is null or empty, return a synthetic TreeNode titled "ROOT" with levelSeq = [].
  2. Create root = createTreeNode(syntheticChainNode("ROOT", [])).
  3. Initialize currentBranch = [root], pending = empty deque.
  4. For each chainNode in chain (in order):
       a. If chainNode is an immediate valid next node of currentBranch.last() (using isImmNext):
             i.   Flush the pending queue into chainNode.content via addNodeToTree in arrival order.
             ii.  Attach chainNode under currentBranch.last() (or root if at root) using addNodeAndUpdateBranch.
             iii. Clear pending.
       b. Else:
             i.   Push chainNode onto the pending queue.
             ii.  If pending.size() == 3:
                  - If isAllNotImmNodesSiblings(pending) is true, attach all three pending nodes as
                    immediate siblings under the nearest suitable ancestor (in queue order), updating
                    currentBranch to end at the last attached node.
                  - Else, merge the oldest pending node's content into the current branch tail's
                    content, then remove it from the queue.
  5. After the loop, merge any remaining pending nodes into currentBranch.last().content in arrival order.
  6. Return root.
Related Features: addNodeAndUpdateBranch, addNodeToTree, createTreeNode, isAllNotImmNodesSiblings,
                  isImmNext, levelSeq, pending queue, currentBranch
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, BaseNode
Input:
  - chain (List<ChainNode>): ordered list of parsed headings produced by ChainParser.parseToChain.
Output:
  - TreeNode: synthetic-rooted outline tree reflecting auto-prune tolerant reconstruction rules.
Pre-condition:
  - Each ChainNode in chain has a well-formed levelSeq list (possibly empty for the synthetic root).
Post-condition:
  - The returned TreeNode has title "ROOT", levelSeq = [], and a children list whose subtree represents
    all headings from `chain`; pending nodes have been merged into content where attachment failed.
  - All parent-child links are consistent.

AutoPruneStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary: Creates a fresh TreeNode whose fields are populated from a ChainNode's data.
Algorithm:
  1. Instantiate a new TreeNode.
  2. Copy chainnode.title -> node.title.
  3. Copy chainnode.levelText -> node.levelText.
  4. Copy chainnode.levelSeq -> node.levelSeq (list is shared or copied to preserve independence).
  5. Copy chainnode.content -> node.content.
  6. Initialize node.children = [] and node.parent = null.
  7. Return node.
Related Features: title, levelText, levelSeq, content, children, parent
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, BaseNode
Input:
  - chainnode (ChainNode): source heading node produced by the parser.
Output:
  - TreeNode: a newly allocated TreeNode mirroring chainnode's textual/numeric data with empty children
    and null parent.
Pre-condition: chainnode must not be null.
Post-condition: Returned TreeNode is detached (parent == null) and has no children.

AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeToTree
Summary: Attaches a parsed chain node to a designated parent in the tree and extends the current branch
         accordingly; pending nodes queued before the current node are merged into the current node's content.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a TreeNode from the chain node via createTreeNode(chainnode).
  2. While the pending queue is non-empty:
       a. Pop the oldest pending chain node.
       b. Append its title (and existing content, if any) to the new TreeNode's content using
          BaseNode.concatNode semantics, preserving arrival order without extra separators.
  3. If currentNodeRef is null or represents the synthetic root, attach the new TreeNode as a child of the
     root node in the tree built by buildTree.
  4. Otherwise, call currentNodeRef.addChild(newTreeNode) and set newTreeNode.parent = currentNodeRef.
  5. Update currentBranch so that its last element is the newTreeNode.
Related Features: createTreeNode, pending queue (held by buildTree), addChild, parent, levelSeq
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, BaseNode
Input:
  - node (ChainNode): the chain node being attached.
  - currentBranch (List<TreeNode>): the running root-to-leaf branch; updated in place.
  - currentNodeRef (node): reference to the nearest ancestor TreeNode under which `node` should be attached.
Output: void
Pre-condition:
  - node must be an immediate valid next node of the TreeNode pointed to by currentNodeRef (per isImmNext),
    unless currentNodeRef is the root.
  - The pending queue must contain zero or more chain nodes whose stored order matches arrival order.
Post-condition:
  - newTreeNode.parent links to currentNodeRef (or root) and currentNodeRef.children contains newTreeNode.
  - All previously pending chain nodes have their content concatenated into newTreeNode.content.
  - currentBranch ends with newTreeNode.

AutoPruneStrategy::isAllNotImmNodesSiblings
Summary: Checks whether all chain nodes currently buffered in the pending queue form an immediate
         sibling sequence (i.e., each consecutive pair satisfies the immediate-next relation).
Algorithm:
  1. If queue has fewer than 2 elements, return false.
  2. For each consecutive pair (a, b) in queue order:
       - Compute isImm = isImmNext(a.levelSeq, b.levelSeq).
       - If any pair is not immediate-next, return false.
  3. Return true.
Related Features: pending queue, isImmNext, levelSeq
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, BaseNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input:
  - queue (Deque): pending chain nodes held by buildTree, in arrival order.
Output:
  - void / boolean: true if every consecutive pair of pending nodes is an immediate valid next pair;
    false otherwise.
Pre-condition: queue must contain only ChainNode instances with non-null levelSeq.
Post-condition: The pending queue is left unchanged.

AutoPruneStrategy::addNodeAndUpdateBranch
Summary: Appends a chain node to the latest valid branch of the partially built tree and updates the branch
         to reflect the new tail, using the auto-prune tolerance rules.
Algorithm:
  1. If the current branch is empty, set it to [rootNode] and return.
  2. Let lastBranchNode = currentBranch.last().
  3. If lastBranchNode is an immediate valid next node of the new node (using TreeBuildingStrategy.isImmNext),
     call addNodeToTree(node, currentBranch, lastBranchNode).
  4. Otherwise, find the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is a proper prefix of node.levelSeq
     (searching backward through currentBranch). Attach node as child of that ancestor, then set
     currentBranch = path(root -> ancestor -> node).
Related Features: addNodeToTree, isImmNext, levelSeq, currentBranch (external state held by buildTree)
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input:
  - node (ChainNode): the incoming parsed heading to be appended.
  - currentBranch (List<TreeNode>): the in-progress root-to-leaf path maintained by buildTree, may be empty.
Output: void
Pre-condition:
  - currentBranch, when non-empty, must represent a valid chain of ancestors from the root TreeNode
    whose concatenated level sequences form a prefix-closed sequence.
  - node must have a non-null levelSeq.
Post-condition:
  - The currentBranch is updated so its last element is the tree node created from `node`
    (or the merge target when an immediate-next relation is detected and pending nodes are consumed).
  - The tree maintained by buildTree is consistent with the new branch.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
StrictStrategy::buildTree
Summary: Reconstructs the document outline tree from a chain of heading nodes using strict rules:
         any chain that does not begin at the root or violates parent-child extension is rejected.
Algorithm:
  1. If chain is null or empty, return a synthetic TreeNode titled "ROOT" with levelSeq = [].
  2. Create root = createTreeNode(syntheticChainNode("ROOT", [])).
  3. Initialize currentBranch = [root].
  4. For each chainNode in chain:
       a. If isRoot(chainNode) (levelSeq is empty):
             - Reject: throw IllegalStateException("Chain must not contain explicit root nodes").
       b. Else if isImmNext(currentBranch.last().levelSeq, chainNode.levelSeq):
             - Attach via currentBranch.last().addChild(newNode); push newNode onto currentBranch.
       c. Else if isChild(currentBranch.last().levelSeq, chainNode.levelSeq):
             - Find the nearest ancestor whose levelSeq is a prefix of chainNode.levelSeq; attach
               underneath that ancestor and update currentBranch.
       d. Else:
             - Reject: throw IllegalStateException("Strict strategy cannot recover from irregular chain").
  5. Return root.
Related Features: createTreeNode, isImmNext, isChild, isRoot, levelSeq
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, BaseNode, TreeBuildingStrategy
Input:
  - chain (List<ChainNode>): ordered list of parsed headings.
Output:
  - TreeNode: synthetic-rooted tree reflecting strict hierarchy.
Pre-condition:
  - chain begins with a node whose levelSeq is a valid child extension of the synthetic root sequence [].
  - Every subsequent node either extends its parent or advances to an immediate next sibling level.
Post-condition:
  - Returned TreeNode has title "ROOT" and children that mirror the chain; no pending/merge logic applied.
  - If the chain violates strict rules, an exception is thrown and no partial tree is returned.

StrictStrategy::createTreeNode
Summary: Creates a fresh TreeNode whose fields are populated from a ChainNode's data, mirroring the
         auto-prune factory semantics.
Algorithm:
  1. Instantiate a new TreeNode.
  2. Copy chainnode.title, chainnode.levelText, chainnode.levelSeq, chainnode.content into the new node.
  3. Initialize node.children = [] and node.parent = null.
  4. Return node.
Related Features: title, levelText, levelSeq, content, children, parent
Related Classes: ChainNode, TreeNode, BaseNode
Input:
  - chainnode (ChainNode): source heading node.
Output:
  - TreeNode: a new detached TreeNode mirroring chainnode's textual/numeric data.
Pre-condition: chainnode must not be null.
Post-condition: Returned TreeNode has no parent and no children.

StrictStrategy::isChild
Summary: Determines whether `childSeq` represents a valid one-level child extension of `parentSeq`
         according to the level-sequence relation rules.
Algorithm:
  1. If parentSeq is empty and childSeq has exactly one element, return true (direct child of root).
  2. If childSeq.size() != parentSeq.size() + 1, return false.
  3. For i in [0, parentSeq.size() - 1], verify childSeq[i] == parentSeq[i]; if any mismatch, return false.
  4. Return true.
Related Features: levelSeq
Related Classes: BaseNode, ChainNode, TreeNode
Input:
  - parentSeq (List<EIntegerObject>): candidate parent level sequence.
  - childSeq (List<EIntegerObject>): candidate child level sequence.
Output:
  - boolean: true if childSeq strictly extends parentSeq by one element with a matching prefix;
    false otherwise.
Pre-condition: Neither argument is null; sequences contain comparable integer values.
Post-condition: No state is mutated.

```text
Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. # Operation Specifications
```
PatternBuilder::validate
Summary: Validates that the builder's current configuration is internally consistent before build()
         is allowed to construct a LevelPattern.
Algorithm:
  1. Assert numberType is non-null.
  2. Assert prefixRegex and suffixRegex (if used) are non-null and syntactically plausible as regex fragments.
  3. Assert 1 <= minLevel <= maxLevel.
  4. Assert separator is either null or a non-empty string used to delimit sub-levels.
  5. If any check fails, throw IllegalStateException (or a domain-specific exception) with a descriptive
     message.
Related Features: numberType, prefixRegex, suffixRegex, separator, minLevel, maxLevel
Related Classes: PatternBuilder
Input: none (operates on instance state).
Output: void
Pre-condition: builder instance has been populated by the caller.
Post-condition: builder is guaranteed to be in a state acceptable to build(); on failure, an exception
                is raised and the builder is left unchanged.

PatternBuilder::modify
Summary: Returns a copy of this builder with the prefix regex and minimum level replaced, enabling
         fluent derivation of slightly different patterns (e.g., for dotted vs undotted numbering).
Algorithm:
  1. Create a copy via copySelf().
  2. On the copy, set prefixRegex = newPrefixRegex and minLevel = newMinLevel.
  3. Return the copy.
Related Features: prefixRegex, minLevel, copySelf
Related Classes: PatternBuilder, LevelPattern
Input:
  - newPrefixRegex (String): replacement prefix regex fragment.
  - newMinLevel (int): new minimum level value (>= 1).
Output:
  - PatternBuilder: a new builder instance reflecting the requested modifications.
Pre-condition: newPrefixRegex is non-null; newMinLevel >= 1.
Post-condition: The original builder remains unchanged; the returned builder carries the new values.

PatternBuilder::copySelf
Summary: Produces a deep copy of this PatternBuilder so callers can derive variants without mutating
         the original configuration.
Algorithm:
  1. Instantiate a new PatternBuilder.
  2. Copy each of numberType, prefixRegex, suffixRegex, separator, minLevel, maxLevel, helper reference
     from this builder to the new instance.
  3. Return the new PatternBuilder.
Related Features: numberType, prefixRegex, suffixRegex, separator, minLevel, maxLevel
Related Classes: PatternBuilder, LevelPattern
Input: none.
Output:
  - PatternBuilder: an independent builder with identical configuration state.
Pre-condition: none.
Post-condition: Mutating the returned builder must not affect the original builder's state.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.
```

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

Post-condition: Returned TreeNode reflects the strategy's interpretation of chain.

# Operation Specifications
ChainParser::createChainNode
Summary: Factory method that constructs a ChainNode carrying the heading's title, content,
         level sequence, original level text, and the matched pattern's priority.
Algorithm:
  1. Instantiate a new ChainNode.
  2. Set node.levelSeq = levelSeq.
  3. Set node.title = title.
  4. Set node.content = content.
  5. Set node.levelText = levelText.
  6. Set node.patternPriority = patternPriority.
  7. Return node.
Related Features: levelSeq, title, content, levelText, patternPriority
Related Classes: ChainNode, BaseNode
Input:
  - levelSeq (List<int>): the parsed integer level sequence for the heading.
  - title (String): the heading title text (heading line minus the level marker).
  - content (String): the initial content text (typically empty for headings).
  - levelText (String): the original numbering text as it appeared in the source line.
  - patternPriority (int): the priority index of the matching LevelPattern.
Output:
  - ChainNode: a fully populated heading node ready for tree construction.
Pre-condition: levelSeq, title, levelText, and patternPriority are non-null where applicable.
Post-condition: Returned ChainNode is detached and independent from input lists (defensive copy assumed).

ChainParser::parseToChain
Summary: Parses a full multi-line document into an ordered list of ChainNode instances by splitting
         the text into lines and delegating each line to detectLevel.
Algorithm:
  1. If text is null or empty, return an empty list.
  2. Split text on newline boundaries into lines (preserving order, dropping trailing empty lines
     produced solely by terminal newline as appropriate).
  3. For each line, invoke detectLevel(line) and append the returned ChainNode to the result list.
  4. Return the accumulated list.
Related Features: patterns, detectLevel
Related Classes: ChainNode, LevelPattern
Input:
  - text (String): the full document text; may contain "\n" (and optionally "\r\n") line breaks.
Output:
  - List<ChainNode>: ordered chain nodes, one per non-empty input line in sequence.
Pre-condition: ChainParser has been constructed with a non-empty pattern list.
Post-condition: Result list contains exactly one ChainNode per processed line, preserving order.

ChainParser::detectLevel
Summary: Attempts to recognize a single line as a heading by trying registered LevelPattern instances
         in priority order; returns a ChainNode for the first valid match, or a content-only ChainNode
         if no pattern matches.
Algorithm:
  1. For each pattern in patterns (in order):
       a. Compile/retrieve pattern.getRegex().
       b. Run matcher against `line`.
       c. If matcher.matches() and !pattern.failOnConvert:
             i.   Convert the matched numbering text via pattern.convertMatchedText(matchedText)
                  into a List<EIntegerObject> (level sequence).
             ii.  If conversion yields a valid sequence (and pattern constraints are satisfied),
                  call createChainNode(levelSeq, title, "", levelText, pattern.priority) and return it.
  2. If no pattern matches, return a content ChainNode with levelSeq = [], title = line, content = line,
     levelText = "", patternPriority = -1 (or sentinel indicating "no match").
Related Features: patterns, regex compilation, matched group extraction, convertMatchedText
Related Classes: ChainNode, LevelPattern, ParserHelper
Input:
  - line (String): a single text line, without trailing newline.
Output:
  - ChainNode: a heading ChainNode when a valid pattern matches, otherwise a content-only ChainNode
    whose title and content both equal `line` and whose levelSeq is empty.
Pre-condition: line is non-null; patterns has been initialized with at least one LevelPattern.
Post-condition: Returned ChainNode captures exactly one logical line interpretation; no state is mutated.

# Operation Specifications
ChainParser::createChainNode
Summary: Factory method that constructs a ChainNode carrying the heading's title, content,
         level sequence, original level text, and the matched pattern's priority.
Algorithm:
  1. Instantiate a new ChainNode.
  2. Set node.levelSeq = levelSeq.
  3. Set node.title = title.
  4. Set node.content = content.
  5. Set node.levelText = levelText.
  6. Set node.patternPriority = patternPriority.
  7. Return node.
Related Features: levelSeq, title, content, levelText, patternPriority
Related Classes: ChainNode, BaseNode
Input:
  - levelSeq (List<int>): the parsed integer level sequence for the heading.
  - title (String): the heading title text (heading line minus the level marker).
  - content (String): the initial content text (typically empty for headings).
  - levelText (String): the original numbering text as it appeared in the source line.
  - patternPriority (int): the priority index of the matching LevelPattern.
Output:
  - ChainNode: a fully populated heading node ready for tree construction.
Pre-condition: levelSeq, title, levelText, and patternPriority are non-null where applicable.
Post-condition: Returned ChainNode is detached and independent from input lists (defensive copy assumed).

ChainParser::parseToChain
Summary: Parses a full multi-line document into an ordered list of ChainNode instances by splitting
         the text into lines and delegating each line to detectLevel.
Algorithm:
  1. If text is null or empty, return an empty list.
  2. Split text on newline boundaries into lines (preserving order, dropping trailing empty lines
     produced solely by terminal newline as appropriate).
  3. For each line, invoke detectLevel(line) and append the returned ChainNode to the result list.
  4. Return the accumulated list.
Related Features: patterns, detectLevel
Related Classes: ChainNode, LevelPattern
Input:
  - text (String): the full document text; may contain "\n" (and optionally "\r\n") line breaks.
Output:
  - List<ChainNode>: ordered chain nodes, one per non-empty input line in sequence.
Pre-condition: ChainParser has been constructed with a non-empty pattern list.
Post-condition: Result list contains exactly one ChainNode per processed line, preserving order.

ChainParser::detectLevel
Summary: Attempts to recognize a single line as a heading by trying registered LevelPattern instances
         in priority order; returns a ChainNode for the first valid match, or a content-only ChainNode
         if no pattern matches.
Algorithm:
  1. For each pattern in patterns (in order):
       a. Compile/retrieve pattern.getRegex().
       b. Run matcher against `line`.
       c. If matcher.matches() and !pattern.failOnConvert:
             i.   Convert the matched numbering text via pattern.convertMatchedText(matchedText)
                  into a List<EIntegerObject> (level sequence).
             ii.  If conversion yields a valid sequence (and pattern constraints are satisfied),
                  call createChainNode(levelSeq, title, "", levelText, pattern.priority) and return it.
  2. If no pattern matches, return a content ChainNode with levelSeq = [], title = line, content = line,
     levelText = "", patternPriority = -1 (or sentinel indicating "no match").
Related Features: patterns, regex compilation, matched group extraction, convertMatchedText
Related Classes: ChainNode, LevelPattern, ParserHelper
Input:
  - line (String): a single text line, without trailing newline.
Output:
  - ChainNode: a heading ChainNode when a valid pattern matches, otherwise a content-only ChainNode
    whose title and content both equal `line` and whose levelSeq is empty.
Pre-condition: line is non-null; patterns has been initialized with at least one LevelPattern.
Post-condition: Returned ChainNode captures exactly one logical line interpretation; no state is mutated.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
TreeNode::mergeAllChildren
Summary: Collapses all immediate children's content into this node's content in document order and
         detaches the children from the tree, producing a leaf node that preserves every descendant's text.
Algorithm:
  1. For each child in this.children in order:
       a. Recursively call child.mergeAllChildren() to flatten the subtree first.
       b. Append child's content into this.content using BaseNode.concatNode semantics (no separator).
  2. Clear this.children.
Related Features: content, children, concatNode
Related Classes: TreeNode, BaseNode
Input: none.
Output: void
Pre-condition: Parent-child links are consistent (no cycles); descendants are reachable only through
               this.children.
Post-condition:
  - this.children is empty (this node becomes a leaf).
  - this.content equals the prior concatenation of this.content and every descendant's content,
    in traversal order, without inserted separators.

TreeNode::getFullContent
Summary: Returns this node's own content followed by the recursively collected content of all
         descendant nodes, concatenated in traversal order without extra separators.
Algorithm:
  1. Initialize result = (this.content == null ? "" : this.content).
  2. For each child in this.children in order:
       - result = result + child.getFullContent().
  3. Return result.
Related Features: content, children
Related Classes: TreeNode, BaseNode
Input: none.
Output:
  - String: the concatenation of this node's content with all descendants' contents in document order.
Pre-condition: Parent-child links are consistent (no cycles).
Post-condition: No state mutation; result is deterministic for the same tree.

TreeNode::addChild
Summary: Registers a child TreeNode under this node and establishes the bidirectional parent link.
Algorithm:
  1. If child is null, return without action.
  2. Set child.parent = this.
  3. Append child to this.children.
Related Features: children, parent
Related Classes: TreeNode, BaseNode
Input:
  - child (TreeNode): node to attach as a direct child.
Output: void
Pre-condition: child must not already be attached to another parent (caller's responsibility).
Post-condition: child.parent == this and child appears in this.children; tree invariants are preserved.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
TreeBuildingStrategy::isRoot
Summary: Determines whether a node represents the synthetic root of the document outline.
Algorithm:
  1. If node is null, return false.
  2. Return node.levelSeq is null OR node.levelSeq.isEmpty().
Related Features: levelSeq
Related Classes: BaseNode, ChainNode, TreeNode
Input:
  - node (BaseNode): candidate node (typically a TreeNode).
Output:
  - boolean: true if the node carries an empty level sequence (the synthetic root marker);
    false otherwise.
Pre-condition: none.
Post-condition: No state is mutated.

TreeBuildingStrategy::getPrefix
Summary: Returns the prefix of a level sequence obtained by removing the last element; the empty
         sequence is returned unchanged.
Algorithm:
  1. If levelSeq is null or empty, return a new empty list.
  2. Else return a new list containing levelSeq[0..size()-2] in order.
Related Features: levelSeq
Related Classes: BaseNode, ChainNode, TreeNode
Input:
  - levelSeq (List<EIntegerObject>): a heading's level sequence.
Output:
  - List<EIntegerObject>: the prefix (original sequence minus its last element), or empty list if
    levelSeq is empty.
Pre-condition: levelSeq elements are comparable and non-null.
Post-condition: Returned list is independent of the input (defensive copy).

TreeBuildingStrategy::getLastLevel
Summary: Returns the last integer value of a level sequence, or 0 when the sequence is empty
         (representing the synthetic root).
Algorithm:
  1. If levelSeq is null or empty, return 0.
  2. Else return levelSeq.get(levelSeq.size() - 1).intValue().
Related Features: levelSeq
Related Classes: BaseNode, ChainNode, TreeNode
Input:
  - levelSeq (List<EIntegerObject>): a heading's level sequence; may be empty.
Output:
  - int: the last level value, or 0 for the empty (root) sequence.
Pre-condition: EIntegerObject elements expose a valid int value.
Post-condition: No state is mutated.

If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

```text
If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.
```

# Operation Specifications
LevelPattern::getRegex
Summary: Lazily compiles and returns the java.util.regex.Pattern that recognizes this pattern's
         heading numbering format in a source line.
Algorithm:
  1. If a cached compiled Pattern is available, return it.
  2. Otherwise, assemble the regex string from regexText (and any helper-derived number pattern from
     helper.getNumberPattern(numberType) if not already embedded).
  3. Wrap the assembled string with start/end anchors as appropriate so the regex matches an entire line.
  4. Compile using Pattern.compile(...) and cache the result.
  5. Return the compiled Pattern.
Related Features: regexText, numberType, helper
Related Classes: LevelPattern, ParserHelper
Input: none (operates on instance state).
Output:
  - Pattern (java.util.regex.Pattern): a compiled regex whose matches correspond to candidate headings
    described by this LevelPattern.
Pre-condition: regexText and helper must be properly initialized; numberType must not be null.
Post-condition: The returned Pattern is cached for subsequent calls.

# Operation Specifications
TreeExporter::nodeToDict
Summary: Converts a TreeNode into a map structure suitable for JSON serialization, exposing the
         required fields: title, level_seq, level_text, content, children.
Algorithm:
  1. Create an EMap.
  2. Put "title"      -> node.title.
  3. Put "level_seq"  -> node.levelSeq (as a list of ints).
  4. Put "level_text" -> node.levelText.
  5. Put "content"    -> node.content.
  6. Put "children"   -> a new list where each child is recursively converted via nodeToDict.
  7. Return the map.
Related Features: title, levelSeq, levelText, content, children
Related Classes: TreeNode, BaseNode
Input:
  - node (TreeNode): node to convert.
Output:
  - EMap: a map keyed by the JSON field names listed above, with children recursively mapped.
Pre-condition: node is non-null.
Post-condition: Returned structure is fully serializable; child order is preserved.

TreeExporter::exportTreeInternal
Summary: Recursive helper that walks the tree depth-first and appends formatted lines for each node.
Algorithm:
  1. Format the current node's line as "LEVEL-" + joined(levelSeq) + ": " + title, then append "\n".
  2. For each child except the last: recurse with prefix + "  ", isLast = false, isRoot = false.
  3. For the last child: recurse with prefix + "  ", isLast = true, isRoot = false.
  4. Return the accumulated string for the subtree rooted at node.
Related Features: levelSeq, title, children, traversal
Related Classes: TreeNode, TreeExporter
Input:
  - node (TreeNode): current node being rendered.
  - prefix (String): indentation prefix inherited from the caller (used for visual hierarchy).
  - isLast (boolean): whether this node is the last child of its parent (influences branch markers).
  - isRoot (boolean): whether this node is the synthetic root (skips indent prefix on the root line).
Output:
  - String: rendered representation of the subtree rooted at node.
Pre-condition: node is non-null; levelSeq is non-null.
Post-condition: Traversal order matches document/source order; output is deterministic.

TreeExporter::exportTree
Summary: Produces a human-readable textual outline of the tree using one line per node, formatted as
         "LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>".
Algorithm:
  1. If tree is null, return "".
  2. Invoke exportTreeInternal(tree, "", true, true) to render the tree.
  3. Return the accumulated string.
Related Features: exportTreeInternal, levelSeq, title
Related Classes: TreeNode, TreeExporter
Input:
  - tree (TreeNode): the outline tree to render.
Output:
  - String: multi-line text, one entry per node, formatted as "LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>" where
    <levelSeq> is the dotted/joined representation of levelSeq elements (e.g., "1.2.3"); empty
    string for a null input.
Pre-condition: tree, when non-null, has consistent parent-child links.

# Requirement
```text
## 1. Overall 

This system turns plain structured text into a document outline tree. It is intended for texts whose section headings are marked by ordered level indicators, such as Arabic numbers, Roman numerals, Chinese numerals, letters, or circled numbers. The main semantic task is to recognize heading lines, convert their numbering into comparable level sequences, preserve ordinary text as section content, and reconstruct the parent-child hierarchy of the document.

## 2. Functional Requirement

Heading recognition is pattern-driven. Patterns are tried in order, and the first valid pattern determines both the heading level sequence and its priority. A line that does not match a valid heading should be treated as content belonging to the current section. Even an empty or unmatched document should still produce a synthetic root section titled `"ROOT"`.

Number conversion should treat each supported numbering family according to its natural ordering. Roman numerals should be case-insensitive and support standard subtractive forms. Chinese numerals should support common simplified and traditional digit variants, units, large magnitudes, and signed values. Letters map alphabetically, and circled numbers map to their represented numeric value. Invalid numeric text should not create a valid heading level.

Tree construction is based on the integer level sequence of each parsed heading. A root node has an empty sequence. A child sequence extends its parent sequence, while siblings share the same prefix and advance by level order. Strict construction should reject chains that do not begin with the root. The more tolerant construction strategy should recover from irregular jumps by moving back to the nearest suitable ancestor before attaching the next node.For the auto-prune strategy, the builder should maintain the latest valid branch from the root to the current node. If the next chain node is an immediate valid next node according to the level-sequence relation, it should be attached to the nearest ancestor whose level sequence is the prefix of the new node, and the current branch should be updated.

If a chain node is not an immediate valid next node, it should be stored in a pending queue rather than attached immediately. When a later immediate node is found, pending nodes before it should be merged into the current node's content in arrival order. If the pending queue reaches three nodes, the strategy should check whether all pending nodes form an immediate sibling sequence. If so, they should be attached to the tree in order; otherwise, the oldest pending node should be merged into the current node's content. After all input nodes are processed, any remaining pending nodes should be merged into the current node's content.

When section content is merged or collected from descendants, content should be concatenated in traversal order without inserting extra separators. Parent-child links should remain consistent when tree nodes are attached.

Export behavior must be deterministic. Chain export should use one line per node in the form `LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>`. Tree JSON export should preserve child order and use the field names `title`, `level_seq`, `level_text`, `content`, and `children`, with stable pretty-printing using four-space indentation.

## 3. External / Tool Classes

`Utils` is an external numeric utility used by the parser for Roman numeral and Chinese numeral conversion.
```

# Operation Specifications
TreeExporter::nodeToDict
Summary: Converts a TreeNode into a map structure suitable for JSON serialization, exposing the
         required fields: title, level_seq, level_text, content, children.
Algorithm:
  1. Create an EMap.
  2. Put "title"      -> node.title.
  3. Put "level_seq"  -> node.levelSeq (as a list of ints).
  4. Put "level_text" -> node.levelText.
  5. Put "content"    -> node.content.
  6. Put "children"   -> a new list where each child is recursively converted via nodeToDict.
  7. Return the map.
Related Features: title, levelSeq, levelText, content, children
Related Classes: TreeNode, BaseNode
Input:
  - node (TreeNode): node to convert.
Output:
  - EMap: a map keyed by the JSON field names listed above, with children recursively mapped.
Pre-condition: node is non-null.
Post-condition: Returned structure is fully serializable; child order is preserved.

TreeExporter::exportTreeInternal
Summary: Recursive helper that walks the tree depth-first and appends formatted lines for each node.
Algorithm:
  1. Format the current node's line as "LEVEL-" + joined(levelSeq) + ": " + title, then append "\n".
  2. For each child except the last: recurse with prefix + "  ", isLast = false, isRoot = false.
  3. For the last child: recurse with prefix + "  ", isLast = true, isRoot = false.
  4. Return the accumulated string for the subtree rooted at node.
Related Features: levelSeq, title, children, traversal
Related Classes: TreeNode, TreeExporter
Input:
  - node (TreeNode): current node being rendered.
  - prefix (String): indentation prefix inherited from the caller (used for visual hierarchy).
  - isLast (boolean): whether this node is the last child of its parent (influences branch markers).
  - isRoot (boolean): whether this node is the synthetic root (skips indent prefix on the root line).
Output:
  - String: rendered representation of the subtree rooted at node.
Pre-condition: node is non-null; levelSeq is non-null.
Post-condition: Traversal order matches document/source order; output is deterministic.

TreeExporter::exportTree
Summary: Produces a human-readable textual outline of the tree using one line per node, formatted as
         "LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>".
Algorithm:
  1. If tree is null, return "".
  2. Invoke exportTreeInternal(tree, "", true, true) to render the tree.
  3. Return the accumulated string.
Related Features: exportTreeInternal, levelSeq, title
Related Classes: TreeNode, TreeExporter
Input:
  - tree (TreeNode): the outline tree to render.
Output:
  - String: multi-line text, one entry per node, formatted as "LEVEL-<levelSeq>: <title>" where
    <levelSeq> is the dotted/joined representation of levelSeq elements (e.g., "1.2.3"); empty
    string for a null input.
Pre-condition: tree, when non-null, has consistent parent-child links.
Post-condition: Output is deterministic for the same tree shape and content.

TreeExporter::exportToJsonFile
Summary: Serializes the given outline tree to JSON and writes the result to a file at the supplied path.
Algorithm:
  1. If tree is null, throw IllegalArgumentException.
  2. Compute json = exportToJson(tree).
  3. Open filePath for writing (UTF-8), write json, and close the stream.
  4. On I/O failure, propagate as IOException.
Related Features: exportToJson, filePath handling
Related Classes: TreeNode, TreeExporter
Input:
  - tree (TreeNode): the outline tree to serialize.
  - filePath (Path): destination file path (may be relative or absolute).
Output: void
Pre-condition:
  - filePath's parent directory exists and is writable, or the runtime is permitted to create it.
Post-condition: A UTF-8 encoded JSON file is created/overwritten at filePath containing the serialized tree.

```java
        }
```

```java
   *   1. If chain is null or empty, return a synthetic TreeNode titled "ROOT" with levelSeq = [].
   *   2. Create root = createTreeNode(syntheticChainNode("ROOT", [])).
```
```java
   *   3. Initialize currentBranch = [root], pending = empty deque.
   *   4. For each chainNode in chain (in order):

   *              i.   Flush the pending queue into chainNode.content via addNodeToTree in arrival order.
   *              ii.  Attach chainNode under currentBranch.last() (or root if at root) using addNodeAndUpdateBranch.
   *              iii. Clear pending.
   *        b. Else:
   *              i.   Push chainNode onto the pending queue.
   *              ii.  If pending.size() == 3:

   *                     immediate siblings under the nearest suitable ancestor (in queue order), updating
   *                     currentBranch to end at the last attached node.
   *                   - Else, merge the oldest pending node's content into the current branch tail's
   *                     content, then remove it from the queue.
   *   5. After the loop, merge any remaining pending nodes into currentBranch.last().content in arrival order.
   *   6. Return root.
   * Related Features: addNodeAndUpdateBranch, addNodeToTree, createTreeNode, isAllNotImmNodesSiblings,
   *                   isImmNext, levelSeq, pending queue, currentBranch
```

```java
   *   4. For each chainNode in chain (in order):

   *              ii.  Attach chainNode under currentBranch.last() (or root if at root) using addNodeAndUpdateBranch.
   *              iii. Clear pending.
   *        b. Else:
   *              i.   Push chainNode onto the pending queue.
   *              ii.  If pending.size() == 3:

   *                     immediate siblings under the nearest suitable ancestor (in queue order), updating
   *                     currentBranch to end at the last attached node.
   *                   - Else, merge the oldest pending node's content into the current branch tail's
   *                     content, then remove it from the queue.
   *   5. After the loop, merge any remaining pending nodes into currentBranch.last().content in arrival order.
   *   6. Return root.
   * Related Features: addNodeAndUpdateBranch, addNodeToTree, createTreeNode, isAllNotImmNodesSiblings,
```

            ChainNode firstPending = pending.peekFirst();

              TreeNode attachParent = branchForAttach.get(branchForAttach.size() - 1);

              }
              else

                attachParent.addChild(newTN);
                newTN.setParent(attachParent);
              }
              branchForAttach.add(newTN);
              // Replace newBranch with branchForAttach
              newBranch = branchForAttach;
            }
            // Replace currentBranch with newBranch
            currentBranch.clear();
            for (TreeNode n : newBranch)

            }

  /**
   * Helper: check if seqA is a proper prefix of seqB.
   */
  private boolean isProperPrefix(EList<Integer> seqA, EList<Integer> seqB)
  {
    if (seqA == null || seqB == null)
    {
      return false;
    }
    if (seqA.size() >= seqB.size())
    {
      return false;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < seqA.size(); i++)
    {
      if (!seqA.get(i).equals(seqB.get(i)))
      {
        return false;
      }
    }
    return true;
  }

  /**
   * Helper: find the path from root to the given target in the tree.
   */
  private TreeNode[] findPath(TreeNode root, TreeNode target)
  {
    java.util.List<TreeNode> path = new java.util.ArrayList<TreeNode>();
    if (findPathHelper(root, target, path))
    {
      return path.toArray(new TreeNode[path.size()]);
    }
    // Fallback: just return root
    return new TreeNode[] { root };
  }

  private boolean findPathHelper(TreeNode current, TreeNode target, java.util.List<TreeNode> path)
  {
    path.add(current);
    if (current == target)
    {
      return true;
    }
    for (TreeNode child : current.getChildren())
    {
      if (findPathHelper(child, target, path))
      {
        return true;
      }
    }
    path.remove(path.size() - 1);
    return false;
  }

  public void addNodeToTree(final ChainNode node, final EList<TreeNode> currentBranch, final TreeNode[] currentNodeRef)
  {
    // Step 1: Create a TreeNode from the chain node
    TreeNode newTreeNode = createTreeNode(node);

    // Step 2: While pending queue is non-empty - merge pending nodes' content into newTreeNode
    // (The pending queue is passed via currentBranch in this context; per the algorithm,
    // we need to consume pending items stored externally. Since the signature only provides
    // currentBranch and currentNodeRef, we use the convention that pending items are tracked
    // through the currentBranch's second-to-last element if available, or simply note that

      newTreeNode.setParent(currentNodeRef[0]);

    currentBranch.add(newTreeNode);
